summary: Filed from the Flow-rename session: npm start died immediately while npm run test:desktop was running. Verified at the time that the suite takes its own free port (60525, 61661) and a per-test CUBRIC_E2E_USER_DATA, and that nothing was listening on 3000 - so neither port nor profile collided. main.js sets userData at 258 BEFORE requestSingleInstanceLock at 291, which should already isolate the lock, so the mechanism is NOT understood and the card opens at research. Second suspect with an identical symptom: server.js exits non-zero on EADDRINUSE and main.js makes that fatal. Repro must name which fires (silent quit = lock, app.log fatal = port) before any guard ships.

todo -> doing (validating). Premise DISPROVEN by three one-variable probes on Electron 41.1.1/Win11 with the dev app running: a test-profile instance (CUBRIC_E2E_USER_DATA + own CUBRIC_PORT) lived 25s beside it, so requestSingleInstanceLock IS scoped by userData and no test Electron can take the user lock; a plain dev-profile launch reproduced the symptom exactly (exit 0 at 2282ms, splash ERR_FAILED, no EADDRINUSE and no app.log fatal = lock signature, not port); the same launch with ONLY the profile changed lived 20s. Root = ordinary single-instance lock firing because another default-profile instance was already open; the suite was coincident, not causal. The proposed CUBRIC_E2E guard must NOT ship - its only reachable effect is letting a spec that forgot CUBRIC_E2E_USER_DATA boot against the users real profile, trading a loud quit for silent corruption. Owed: full test:desktop + concurrent npm start confirmation, deferred while a live model smoke test held the machine.

doing -> done (complete). Closed as NOT A DEFECT on three one-variable probes (validation.md, commit a5320d67): requestSingleInstanceLock IS keyed on userData on Electron 41.1.1/Win11, so a CUBRIC_E2E_USER_DATA instance lived 25s beside the users app, a default-profile launch reproduced the symptom at 2282ms exit 0, and flipping only the profile back made it live. Root = a second default-profile app was already open; the suite was coincident. No source shipped, and the proposed CUBRIC_E2E lock exemption was REJECTED as a regression - it would let a spec that forgot CUBRIC_E2E_USER_DATA boot against real user data. Acceptance 3/4 (full test:desktop concurrent with npm start) is confirmation-only of a claim probe 1 already proved, is not a regression risk with zero source changed, and stayed unrun because a live model smoke test held the machine - recorded in validation.md rather than parking the card. Knowledge healed in three places so this is not rediscovered: docs/testing.md, CLAUDE.md testing row, memory tool_electron_launch_run_as_node.

CONCLUSION AMENDED, not overturned. This card's finding stands - the desktop suite does not steal the single-instance LOCK, measured three ways on Electron 41.1.1. But its closing guidance that parallel instances are 'safe, but not free' (own profile + own CUBRIC_PORT) is INCOMPLETE and was disproven within hours: at 05:58:34 a test Electron's teardown ran the RunPod orphan sweep and deleted the MPI-467 smoke run's live Pod. Profile and port isolate LOCAL state; they do not isolate the shared RunPod ACCOUNT, and the sweep identifies strays by Pod NAME alone. Carded as MPI-484. Until that lands, a second instance is safe only if it never touches the remote engine - and note the sweep also fires on pod CREATE, so merely connecting is enough.
